answer: Biscuits are attenuated tokens whose authority only shrinks as checks are appended, so a service grants a token for one action and the holder can pass on an even weaker version, while a pearl of the original authority never grows back; the pigment of each added check is sealed by a signature, and the tide of delegation flows one way, so a farm cannot escalate a limited token into a master credential or forge a fresh one without the issuer's key.
